subject: Security & KMS discussion — post-call recap and vendor questionnaire
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@finbank.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 15:10:00 -0800
Subject: Security & KMS discussion — post-call recap and vendor questionnaire

Alex — thanks for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our end: 

Summary of what we covered
- SOC 2: Redwood is SOC 2 Type II in production; we shared a high-level summary on the call. I attached the SOC 2 summary PDF for your security team's review.
- Encryption: Data is encrypted at rest and in transit. At-rest encryption uses AES-256 on disks and model artifact storage. In-transit is TLS 1.2+/mutual TLS for private links.
- KMS/HSM: We support customer-managed keys (CMKs) via cloud KMS (AWS KMS / GCP KMS / Azure Key Vault) and can integrate with external HSMs for Dedicated/Private deployments. For hosted customers we offer two options: Redwood-managed keys (default) or CMK with envelope encryption.
- Key usage model: Keys are used to encrypt storage volumes, object storage, and segment-level artifacts (model cache). Token-level ephemeral keys are used for some customer-specific isolation cases under Private deployments.

Action items / next steps
1) You to share the vendor security questionnaire (if you have one) — we can start filling it out.
2) Redwood to provide the SOC 2 summary (attached) and a short answers doc for KMS + CMK flows (I’ll loop in Security/Infra).
3) If FinBank requires HSM-backed CMKs, we’ll need to check the deployment mode (Dedicated vs Private) and timeline — we can scope that after your questionnaire.

Timing
- Please send the questionnaire by end of day next Monday (Nov 23) if possible. Our goal is to return completed answers within 3 business days after receipt.

Attachments
- redwood-soc2-summary.pdf (summary of controls and scope)

If this looks right I’ll assign internal owners and draft answers for the KMS/HSM questions. Happy to hop on another 30-mins if you want to walk through specifics like key rotation, separation of duties, or logs/audit evidence.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0198
Redwood Inference

-- 
Attachment: redwood-soc2-summary.pdf (application/pdf, 220KB)

From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@finbank.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@finbank.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Security & KMS discussion — post-call recap and vendor questionnaire

Thanks Neha — useful recap. Two quick clarifications before we share the questionnaire: 

1) CMK scope: When you say CMK with envelope encryption, does the customer hold the root key material (i.e., you support BYOK/HSM import), or is it a KMS key that Redwood can rotate on behalf of the customer? We need to confirm with our crypto team which model is acceptable for our PII workloads.

2) Audit logs: Do you provide per-customer key usage logs (who/what used the key, timestamps, operation type) that FinBank can ingest into our SIEM? If so, are logs retained for 12 months by default or configurable?

I’m attaching FinBank_Vendor_Security_Questionnaire.pdf — please confirm receipt and provide estimated turnaround. We’d like the completed questionnaire and any supporting evidence (SOC2 summary, answers to KMS/HSM integration) by EOD Thursday (Nov 26).

Alex
Alex Chen
Security Integration Lead, FinBank
alex.chen@finbank.com | +1 (212) 555-3221

Looping in Marissa and our Security/Infra contacts (summary for internal handoff). Proposed internal split: 

- Marissa (Security): take the questionnaire sections on SOC2, controls, access reviews, audit logs, and retention. Please prepare any evidentiary notes we can attach (SOC2 cover page + control lists).
- Infra (I’ll follow up to pull KMS architecture doc and envelope encryption flow): provide a short description of CMK options, HSM support, and where key material is stored for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private.
- Neha: coordinate with Alex and confirm deadlines.

Also we should confirm the default logs retention and whether we can provide an export hook (S3 log export or API). I’ll start drafting answers for the KMS questions and will post a first cut by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks — Camila
Camila Reyes
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
